The governing figure is gps_trace.trace_distance_km, not the rounded trip_record.actual_distance_km of 15.1 km, as POL-RD-01 requires.

The rider has discharged the initial burden under POL-RD-08: the trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-02854 and the trace runs from the recorded trip_started event at 2026-09-09T11:59:18+08:00 to trip_completed at 12:18:58+08:00, matching the trip record; and the excess meets the POL-RD-01 threshold on an unimpaired trace (100.0% coverage, 119 fixes, no gaps, max_gap_sec 0.0). The burden now shifts to the driver to point to a specific artifact and clause.

The driver's traffic excuse does not discharge that burden. He asserts 'a massive jam on the expressway, everyone was diverting', but the bundle holds no traffic_advisory covering this trip window: EV-ADVIS-02854-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and no payload, and its own issue detail records that no advisory covers the Blk 231 Serangoon Ave 3 corridor in this window. Under POL-RD-13 the assertion is tested against the traffic_advisory and nothing else; with no advisory on file the POL-RD-03 comparison cannot be run, POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. The driver names no advisory evidence ID, so this is a gap in the bundle, not a POL-RD-10(5) escalation.

No rider-requested detour can excuse any part of the excess. The chat log for this trip is empty — 0 messages, first_message_at and last_message_at both null — so there is no rider instruction meeting POL-RD-04(a) to (c), no waypoint_hint to test against the 200 m corroboration threshold, and no road named. POL-RD-04 is unavailable on this record and no distance is excluded from the excess before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 are applied.

No relocation clause rescues the driver either. The trip_record shows original_pickup and original_dropoff both null, pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at both null, and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min both null. POL-RD-05 therefore cannot be run — there was no amendment to re-quote against — and the booked optimal of 11.8 km stands as the baseline.

The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02, run against the booked optimal because no exculpatory clause reduces the excess. recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 11.8 + 0.28 x 15.9) x 1.0 surge) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP = 17.9020. Charged_total is 21.45, so the refund is 21.45 - 17.9020 = 3.5480, rounded up to SGD 3.55. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and far below the 90% full-refund share, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND. The surge multiplier of 1.0 is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, the only artifact that carries it.

There is accordingly no pass-through correction to add on top of the POL-RD-02 figure, and no billing-integrity defect under POL-RD-09(4). The rider's recovery is the distance-and-time refund alone.

The deviation is not MATERIAL: the excess of 3.26 km is below the 8.0 km absolute materiality threshold and 27.63% is below the 50% threshold, so POL-RD-06 is not engaged and no repeat-deviation pattern test runs. I note for completeness that the driver_profile carries deviation_flags_90d of 1 against completed_trips_90d of 387, which would not meet the POL-RD-06 pattern test in any event, and that prior_deviation_flags is a lifetime counter that POL-GEN-01 forbids substituting for the trailing-90-day figure.

The case is decidable on the present record and should be ruled, not escalated.

ruling.explanation:
This ruling is addressed to both parties.

To the rider: your claim is upheld in part. The platform's GPS trace (EV-GPS-02854) measures 15.06 km between the recorded pickup and dropoff events, against a booked optimal route of 11.8 km on the trip record (EV-TRIP-02854). That is an excess of 3.26 km, or 27.63%. Under POL-RD-01 both establishment tests pass (the excess is more than 20% of the optimal distance, i.e. more than 2.36 km, and more than 0.8 km in absolute terms), so a route deviation is established on this trip's own evidence. POL-RD-01 requires me to use the trace figure (15.06 km) and not the rounded trip-record copy (15.1 km), which I have done.

To the driver: your explanation that there was a jam on the expressway is not something this ruling can act on. POL-RD-13 requires an external-traffic excuse to be tested against the traffic advisory for this trip, and the bundle holds none: EV-ADVIS-02854-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0, and its own record states no advisory covers this corridor in this window. POL-RD-03 is therefore unavailable and your assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. I record that the assertion was discarded and that no advisory was on file. Both of the traffic-excuse claims as drafted were discarded by the referee at the citation stage for failing to disclose the impaired advisory's MISSING_ARTIFACT issue code; that is a citation defect only, and the substantive position they argued is answered here anyway.

On the exculpatory routes generally: the chat log (EV-CHAT-02854) is empty (0 messages), so no rider-requested detour under POL-RD-04 exists and no distance is excluded; the trip record shows no pickup or dropoff amendment and no amended optimal distance, so POL-RD-05 cannot run; and the vehicle type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so POL-RD-12 does not apply and 11.8 km is the correct baseline.

On materiality and the driver's record: the excess (3.26 km / 27.63%) is below the POL-RD-01 materiality figures of 8.0 km and 50%, so POL-RD-06 is not engaged and no repeat-deviation pattern test runs. For completeness, the driver's citable counters (deviation_flags_90d 1 against completed_trips_90d 387) would not meet the POL-RD-06 pattern test in any event; prior_deviation_flags was mentioned by one claim but is a lifetime counter that POL-GEN-01 forbids using as a ground, and it was not used here.

The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02. The fare model is METERED and the surge multiplier read from the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-02854) is 1.0. recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 11.8 + 0.28 x 15.9) x 1.0) + 0.80 platform fee + 0.00 ERP + 0.00 surcharges + 0.00 waiting time - 0.00 promo = 17.902. charged_total is 21.45, so the refund is 21.45 - 17.902 = 3.548, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 = 3.55. That is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis floor and well below the 90% full-refund share (it is 16.5% of the charge), so the outcome is a partial refund.

On pass-through charges: the fare breakdown carries no ERP or toll lines and no airport surcharge, so POL-RD-09 adds nothing on top of the POL-RD-02 figure, and there is no billing-integrity defect to refer. No driver compensation is due: the rider was billed for 15.1 km against a 15.06 km trace, so there is no unbilled-distance shortfall.

No escalation is required. The trace is not impaired for policy purposes (100% coverage, 119 fixes at a 10 s interval, no gaps, max gap 0.0 s), so POL-RD-07(a)-(c) does not fire and no independent corroboration is needed; trip identifiers match across all three artifacts; and the refund is far below the SGD 150.00 ceiling.
